## arch a diagram check that cannot run fails as a tool failure

ID: `lockstep-checks/arch-a-diagram-check-that-cannot-run-fails-as-a-tool-failure`

Status: **implemented and tested**

`lockstep check arch` SHALL report that LikeC4 could not be run, and SHALL NOT report the diagram invalid, when `npx` is absent or cannot be started, when `npx likec4 validate` exits non-zero without LikeC4 having run, or when the JSON export of an already-validated diagram fails. Whether LikeC4 ran SHALL be decided by running it against no diagram, not by matching words in its output. Each of these SHALL print `RESULT arch-<action> tool_unavailable=1 exit=1` and exit 1: a check that did not run must fail, not pass. A diagram LikeC4 read and rejected SHALL still be reported `invalid_diagram=1`.

## arch code imports match the diagram

ID: `lockstep-checks/arch-code-imports-match-the-diagram`

Status: **implemented and tested**

`lockstep check arch check`, when the committed contracts file matches the diagram, SHALL run the contracts against the code with import-linter and exit 1 when any contract is broken, printing the broken contract and the importing module. When import-linter is not installed it SHALL print that and exit 1; it SHALL NOT pass. When the diagram maps no Python packages there is nothing to check, and it SHALL pass without running import-linter.

## arch diagram becomes import contracts

ID: `lockstep-checks/arch-diagram-becomes-import-contracts`

Status: **implemented and tested**

`lockstep check arch gen` SHALL write one import-linter forbidden contract per diagram element that has `python` metadata, forbidding direct imports of every other mapped element it has no relation to. When LikeC4 reports the diagram invalid, it SHALL stop with LikeC4's errors and write no contracts.

## changed a changed statement needs a changed scenario or a wording only declaration

ID: `lockstep-checks/changed-a-changed-statement-needs-a-changed-scenario-or-a-wording-only-declaration`

Status: **implemented and tested**

The changed check SHALL report `no-scenario-changed` and exit 1 when a requirement's statement differs from the base while none of its scenarios is new or different, unless a plan that is new or different from the base lists the requirement ID on a `Wording-only:` line. It SHALL print each wording-only declaration it accepted with the plan's path, and count them in its count line. A `Wording-only:` line MAY list scenario IDs as well as requirement IDs; a requirement ID covers its statement and all its scenarios.

## changed and test first the base is where the branch started

ID: `lockstep-checks/changed-and-test-first-the-base-is-where-the-branch-started`

Status: **implemented and tested**

`lockstep check changed --base <rev>` and `lockstep check test-first --base <rev>` SHALL compare the current revision with the merge base of `<rev>` and the current commit, so that what was merged into `<rev>` after the branch started is not counted as this branch's change. When `<rev>` and the current commit share no history, or the repository has no commit yet, they SHALL compare with `<rev>` itself.

## changed count line and exit status

ID: `lockstep-checks/changed-count-line-and-exit-status`

Status: **implemented and tested**

The changed check SHALL end with the line `RESULT changed requirements=<n> unplanned=<n> no_scenario=<n> wording_only=<n> small=<n> full=<n> no_plan_size=<n> no_planning_package=<n> exit=<0|1>`, exiting 1 when `unplanned`, `no_scenario`, `no_plan_size` or `no_planning_package` is above zero. `small` and `full` SHALL count the listed requirements of each size. When `<rev>` does not name a commit it SHALL check nothing, print `RESULT changed skipped="base <rev> not found" exit=0` and exit 0. `changed` SHALL be a check name in `lockstep.yaml` with the same `block`, `warn` and `off` modes as the other checks.

The changed check SHALL report a listed requirement as `unplanned` and exit 1 when no plan that is new or different from the base revision names it. ## changed every plan that names a listed requirement states its size

ID: `lockstep-checks/changed-every-plan-that-names-a-listed-requirement-states-its-size`

Status: **implemented and tested**

The changed check SHALL read, in each plan that names a listed requirement, every line `Plan size: small` or `Plan size: full` that stands outside a fenced code block: in the `proposal.md` of an OpenSpec change, or in the page itself for a page in `docs/plans/`. A listed requirement's size SHALL be `full` when any plan naming it says `full`, otherwise `small` when one says `small`. The check SHALL report `no-plan-size` and exit 1 for a listed requirement that a plan names when no plan naming it gives a size, and the finding SHALL name the file the line belongs in. For a requirement whose size is `full` it SHALL report `no-planning-package` and exit 1 unless a plan naming it has, outside a fenced code block, a line `Planning package: <path>` (the path with or without backticks) whose path is a file in the repository. It SHALL print each listed requirement's size in its text block and include it in its JSON output. A requirement reported `unplanned` SHALL get no size finding.

## changed requirements that differ from the base are listed with their code and tests

ID: `lockstep-checks/changed-requirements-that-differ-from-the-base-are-listed-with-their-code-and-tests`

Status: **implemented and tested**

`lockstep check changed --base <rev>` SHALL compare the text of every requirement and scenario in the plan at the current revision (`openspec/specs/` with the spec deltas of active changes applied over it) with the plan at the base revision, treating runs of whitespace as one space. It SHALL print, for each requirement that is new, removed, or whose statement or any scenario is new, removed or different: the requirement ID and its kind (`new`, `changed` or `removed`), which parts differ, the symbols whose docstrings implement it, the tests marked for its scenarios, each labelled `changed`, `unchanged` or `new` against the base revision's copy of that test function, and the plan that names it. `--json` SHALL print the same as JSON. It SHALL read the base revision from git without changing the working tree.

## each check can be set to block warn or off in lockstep yaml

ID: `lockstep-checks/each-check-can-be-set-to-block-warn-or-off-in-lockstep-yaml`

Status: **implemented and tested**

`lockstep check <name>` (`trace`, `arch`, `test-first`, `sources`, `docmeta` and the others) SHALL read `checks:` in `lockstep.yaml` at the repository root, where each check is `block` (the default when absent or when there is no file), `warn` or `off`; `maintainability`, `helper-reuse` and `mutation` SHALL instead be `off` when absent, and a bare YAML `on` SHALL mean `block`. A failing `block` check SHALL exit 1; a failing `warn` check SHALL print a `warning:` line and exit 0; an `off` check SHALL not run, SHALL print `skipped (off)` and exit 0. A value other than those three, or an unknown check name, SHALL exit 2 naming it. The file's `sources.human_pattern` (default `brian`), `owner` (no default) and `likec4` (default `1.60.0`) settings SHALL be read from the same file. `lockstep check` with no name, or only `--repo`, `--base` and `--json`, SHALL keep running the whole-tree plan check.

## helper reuse flags a rewrite of an existing function

ID: `lockstep-checks/helper-reuse-flags-a-rewrite-of-an-existing-function`

Status: **implemented and tested**

`lockstep check helper-reuse --base <rev>` SHALL send the index of every function on the merge base and each function the branch adds to a light model through `llm_client`, then judge each new function against up to three named candidates (same_job, partial_overlap, different), and SHALL end with `RESULT helper-reuse new_functions=<n> flagged=<n> cost_usd=<x> exit=<0|1>`, exiting 1 on same_job and 2 when a call or step fails. Its prompt templates SHALL ship inside the Lockstep package.

## instructions the agent chain fits its budget

ID: `lockstep-checks/instructions-the-agent-chain-fits-its-budget`

Status: **implemented and tested**

The instructions check SHALL report `payload_over_cap` when the byte sizes of the chain files that exist (default `~/code2/AGENTS.md`, the project-root file Codex reads above the repository's own; `--chain FILE`, repeatable, or `INSTRUCTION_CHAIN` separated by the path separator, replace it) plus the repository's root `AGENTS.md` add up to more than 32,768 bytes, and `root_oversized` when the root `AGENTS.md` alone is more than 12,000 bytes. The global `~/.codex/AGENTS.md` SHALL NOT be counted, because Codex's budget (`project_doc_max_bytes`) applies to project files only.

## maintainability only findings the branch adds fail

ID: `lockstep-checks/maintainability-only-findings-the-branch-adds-fail`

Status: **implemented and tested**

`lockstep check maintainability --base <rev>` SHALL compare the merge base with the working tree over the Python files under `--folders` (default `src,scripts`) and exit 1 only on a finding the branch adds: a blind `except` or `try/except/pass` (ruff BLE, S110, S112), a function over the complexity limit more complex than on the base (C901), more repeated 6-line windows of code, or a file over `--max-lines` (default 800) that grew. It SHALL end with `RESULT maintainability new=<n> base_findings=<n> head_findings=<n> exit=<0|1>`, SHALL exit 0 with a `skipped=` line when the base is missing or no Python file changed, and SHALL exit 2 when a tool fails.

## mutation survivors are a report and a broken run is a failure

ID: `lockstep-checks/mutation-survivors-are-a-report-and-a-broken-run-is-a-failure`

Status: **implemented and tested**

The mutation check SHALL exit 0 when mutmut finished or was stopped at the time limit, survivors or not, and 2 when mutmut is missing, fails (naming any test that failed in mutmut's copy), gives no results, or was stopped at the limit twice running without fewer mutants left unchecked. A run stopped at the limit SHALL stop mutmut's whole process group, and a results file cut off by the stop SHALL be set aside so mutmut checks those mutants again. In `warn` mode the 2 becomes 0 with a warning, so a nightly run SHALL use `block`.

ID: `lockstep-checks/test-first-a-changed-scenario-needs-a-test-that-fails-before-the-change`

Status: **implemented and tested**

`lockstep check test-first --base <rev>` SHALL, for each scenario that both revisions define and whose text differs (runs of whitespace counting as one space; text from an active change's spec delta replacing the spec's), run every test marked for it against the base revision's source, and SHALL report `no-failing-test <scenario id>` and exit 1 when none of them fails there. It SHALL NOT check a scenario that a plan new or different from the base declares on a `Wording-only:` line, by its own ID or its requirement's. Its count line SHALL add `changed=<n>`, the number of changed scenarios checked, and `no_failing_test=<n>`.

## trace a marked quote matches its requirement

ID: `lockstep-checks/trace-a-marked-quote-matches-its-requirement`

Status: **implemented and tested**

The trace check SHALL read, in every Markdown file tracked by git outside `openspec/`, each passage between `<!-- lockstep quote: <requirement id> -->` and `<!-- /lockstep quote -->`. It SHALL report `stale-quote` and fail when the passage, with runs of whitespace counting as one space, does not appear in the text of that requirement or of one of its scenarios, in `openspec/specs/` or in an active change's spec delta. It SHALL report `unknown` when no spec or active change defines the ID, and `unclosed-quote` when a start marker has no end marker after it in the same file. Each finding SHALL name the file and line of the start marker. A marker inside a code span or a fenced code block is shown as code, not used as a marker, and SHALL be skipped; a passage SHALL be compared with its code words kept. In a folder that is not a git repository it SHALL read every Markdown file outside `openspec/` and folders whose name starts with a dot.

## trace comment lines in configured files implement requirements

ID: `lockstep-checks/trace-comment-lines-in-configured-files-implement-requirements`

Status: **implemented and tested**

The trace check SHALL also read `Implements:` lines in the files, and the files under the folders, listed in `[tool.lockstep] comment_sources` in `pyproject.toml`: a line whose text, after optional leading space and a comment opener (`#`, `{#`, `//` or `<!--`), starts with `Implements:`, naming one or more IDs separated by commas, with any closing `#}` or `-->` removed. A line with no comment opener (such as a docstring line in a `.py.jinja` file) is not read. With no `comment_sources`, no such file is read.
